simple: Pathfinding lets a character find its own way to a spot, walking around walls, jumping gaps, and climbing ladders. You ask `PathfindingService` for a path, and it gives you a list of waypoints to walk to one by one. This is how you make NPCs chase players, guide a pet, or auto-walk a player to a goal. You can also make characters avoid lava or water, skip danger zones, or use a boat.
analogy: It is like a map app on a phone. You say where you want to go, it plans a route around buildings, and if a road gets blocked it finds a new route. Costs are like telling the app to avoid toll roads.
keyPoints: Turn on Navigation mesh and Pathfinding modifiers in the Visualization Options at the top right of the viewport to see where characters can walk.
Create a path with `PathfindingService:CreatePath()`, giving settings like `AgentRadius`, `AgentHeight`, `AgentCanJump`, `AgentCanClimb`, and `Costs`.
Compute it with `path:ComputeAsync(start, finish)` inside `pcall`, then check that `path.Status` is `Enum.PathStatus.Success`.
`path:GetWaypoints()` returns waypoints in order. Each has a `Position` and an `Action`, such as `Jump`.
Listen to `path.Blocked` and recompute only if the blocked waypoint is ahead of the character.
`Costs` make some materials or regions less attractive. Every material costs 1 by default, and `math.huge` means never go there.
A `PathfindingModifier` on an invisible, non-colliding part can mark a region with a `Label`, like `DangerZone`, or let paths pass through with `PassThrough`.
A `PathfindingLink` between two attachments, with a `Label` like `UseBoat`, lets your script do a special action to cross a gap.
Paths fail if they are over 3,000 studs, need over 20,000 nodes, or the agent settings make the goal unreachable.

terms.agent: The character or object that is following the path.
terms.waypoint: One stop along the path. The character walks from waypoint to waypoint, about 4 studs apart by default.
terms.navigation mesh: An invisible map of all the places a character can walk, swim, or jump to.
terms.AgentRadius: How wide the agent is, in studs, measured from its center. Default `2`, so paths stay about 2 studs from walls.
terms.AgentHeight: How tall the agent is, in studs. Default `5`. Gaps lower than this, like under stairs, are treated as blocked.
terms.cost: How much the pathfinder dislikes a material or region. With `Water = 20`, one stud of water counts like 20 studs of grass, so it will go around if it can.
terms.math.huge: A number bigger than any other. As a cost, it means the agent will never go there.
terms.PathfindingModifier: An object you put in a part to label a region or let paths go through it.
terms.PathfindingLink: A shortcut between two attachments that the pathfinder can use, like a boat ride or a teleport pad.
terms.TrussPart: A ladder-like part that characters can climb.
terms.node: A tiny step the pathfinder checks while searching. It gives up after 20,000.
terms.streaming: Loading only the parts of the world near the player. Faraway objects might not exist yet on the player's device.
terms.persistent model: A model that loads soon after joining and never unloads, even with streaming on.

example.title: Make an NPC walk to a goal part
example.place: Script inside an NPC model (with a Humanoid) in Workspace, and a part named Goal in Workspace
example.code:
local PathfindingService = game:GetService("PathfindingService")

local npc = script.Parent
local humanoid = npc:WaitForChild("Humanoid")
local rootPart = npc:WaitForChild("HumanoidRootPart")
local goal = workspace:WaitForChild("Goal")

local path = PathfindingService:CreatePath({
	AgentCanJump = true,
	Costs = {
		Water = 20, -- avoid water when possible
		CrackedLava = math.huge, -- never walk on lava
	},
})

-- Ask for a path from the NPC to the goal
local success, err = pcall(function()
	path:ComputeAsync(rootPart.Position, goal.Position)
end)

if success and path.Status == Enum.PathStatus.Success then
	for _, waypoint in path:GetWaypoints() do
		-- Jump if this waypoint needs it
		if waypoint.Action == Enum.PathWaypointAction.Jump then
			humanoid.Jump = true
		end
		humanoid:MoveTo(waypoint.Position)
		humanoid.MoveToFinished:Wait() -- wait to reach this waypoint
	end
	print("Arrived!")
else
	warn("No path found:", err)
end
explain: We create a path that can jump, avoids water if it can, and never crosses cracked lava.
`ComputeAsync` plans the route from the NPC to the Goal part. It is in `pcall` because it can fail.
If it worked, we loop through each waypoint in order.
If a waypoint says Jump, we make the NPC jump, then `MoveTo` walks it there.
`MoveToFinished:Wait()` pauses until the NPC reaches that waypoint, then the loop moves to the next one.
This simple version does not handle `path.Blocked`. For moving obstacles, connect to it and recompute.

watchOut: Not checking `path.Status`. A path can compute without an error but still have no route.
Computing a path while the character is in the air. Wait until it is on the ground for a better start point.
Using a destination object in a LocalScript that has not streamed in yet. Use a persistent model or do it on the server.
Giving a material `math.huge` cost when you only want it as a last option. Use a big but normal number like `100`.
Ignoring blocked paths in a changing world. Recompute when `path.Blocked` fires ahead of the character.
